description:
Project: Workload-aware batching defaults (Cost Optimization Automation)

Goal
- Ship recommended batching profiles for common latency SLO tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient) so customers and internal services get predictable p95 latency and lower $/1M tokens without manual tuning.
- Make batching behavior “workload-aware” (prompt length distribution, concurrency, streaming vs non-streaming, model family, GPU SKU) and safe-by-default via guardrails and rollout controls.

Scope
- Define the three SLO tiers precisely (targets, typical use-cases, constraints) and map them to runtime batching knobs (e.g., max batch size, max queue delay, prefill/decode scheduling weights, KV cache pressure limits, admission control).
- Implement defaults in the runtime config layer and propagate them through Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployment config surfaces.
- Add telemetry and dashboards to validate tier adherence (p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, batch formation stats, queue delay, GPU utilization, cancellation/timeout rates).
- Build an evaluation+quality gate for batching changes (prompt-set coverage, regression thresholds) and a safe rollout plan (feature flag / gradual enablement / auto-rollback signals).
- Update docs/SDK examples and Redwood Optimize messaging so the feature is discoverable and customers understand trade-offs.

Non-goals (initial release)
- Fully automated per-customer bespoke batching optimization (beyond the three tiers).
- New scheduling algorithm research; focus is productizing and hardening tiered defaults with limited new heuristics.

Stakeholders / teams
- Product (Optimize): Aditya Rao (DRI), with input from Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API) and Henry Cho.
- Serving Runtime: Mateo Alvarez (exec sponsor), Sofia Ivanova (runtime scheduling), Omar El‑Sayed / Lena Fischer / Marcus Reed.
- Applied ML & Evals: Dr. Maya Srinivasan / Jonas Weber, with Arjun Desai + Hassan Mirza for characterization and guardrails.
- SRE/Infra/Observability: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes / Allison Grant for SLO definitions, dashboards, and safe rollout.
- DevEx/Docs/SDKs: Alex Martinez / Monica Patel for docs and SDK-facing examples (no breaking API changes).
- Release Engineering: Connor O’Brien for release train coordination.

Timeline (plausible)
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): Data gathering + tier definition; draft PRD/spec; identify launch models/regions.
- Phase 1 (2–3 weeks): Runtime implementation behind a flag; add instrumentation; build perf canary coverage.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): Evals/guardrails + dashboards; internal dogfooding.
- Phase 3 (1–2 weeks): Limited beta (subset of models/regions) + staged rollout; docs and release notes.
- Phase 4 (ongoing): Tune defaults per model family/GPU SKU; expand to more regions; incorporate customer feedback.

Key deliverables
- Confluence PRD + design spec + ADRs.
- Linear initiative with execution tickets (runtime, SRE, evals, docs).
- GitHub PRs implementing: tier config schema, runtime batching policy selection, instrumentation, perf canaries, docs updates.
- Slack coordination threads (runtime/product/SRE) and incident-style threads if regressions occur.
- Drive working docs: benchmark spreadsheets, rollout checklists, meeting notes.
- Optional customer artifacts: a few sales/SE calls, CRM notes, and support tickets to reflect real-world feedback.

Constraints / risks
- Tail-latency risk if queue-delay defaults are too aggressive; must couple with overload protection and clear auto-rollback thresholds.
- Model-family differences (context length, prefill cost, quantization) can change optimal batching; defaults must be parameterized and benchmarked.
- Streaming workloads are sensitive to batching; tiering must not degrade token cadence.
- Must remain backwards compatible: existing explicit batching configs should override tier defaults.

files.description: PRD defining user problems, tier definitions (fast/standard/cost-efficient), success metrics ($/token, p95), rollout plan, and customer-facing positioning for batching defaults.
Detailed design spec: config surfaces, runtime selection logic, precedence rules (explicit config vs tier default), migration strategy, and edge cases (streaming, long-context, tool-calls).
ADR documenting why Redwood is standardizing on three batching tiers, how targets were chosen, and the decision on which knobs are controlled by defaults vs customer override.
Performance standards update: definitions for queue delay metrics, batch formation KPIs, and acceptable regressions per tier; guidance for reviewers on batching-related changes.
Runtime implementation notes: scheduler hooks, tier-to-parameter mapping, admission control integration, and model/GPU-specific overrides.
Methodology for benchmarking tiered profiles: workload corpus selection, concurrency sweeps, streaming cadence checks, and how results map to go/no-go thresholds.
Definition of representative workload corpus (prompt length histograms, multi-turn chat traces, long-context, embeddings) used for both perf and quality regression checks.
Quality guardrails for batching changes: prompt-set eval requirements, acceptable deltas, sampling methodology, and automated rollback triggers tied to A/B or canary.
SRE doc defining SLO tier targets (p95/p99), measurement windows, error budget policy, and how tiered batching impacts paging/alerts.
Dashboards/alerts spec: per-tier latency, queue delay, batch size distributions, GPU util, timeout/cancel rates; includes alert thresholds and ownership.
Docs plan outlining customer documentation updates (API config examples, migration notes), plus SDK example changes and FAQ on trade-offs.
Beta release notes: feature flag, supported models/regions, known limitations, how to opt in/out, and what telemetry customers can use to validate tier behavior.
Runtime release notes describing scheduler changes, new metrics, configuration schema changes, and compatibility notes for Dedicated/Private.
PM ticket for the launch plan: milestones, beta cohort definition, comms checklist, and alignment with Optimize roadmap.
PM task to finalize tier definitions, customer-facing names, and documentation requirements; includes review checklist with SRE and DevEx.
Engineering ticket to add tier selection to runtime config schema, including precedence rules and validation.
Engineering ticket for runtime logic selecting batching parameters based on tier + workload signals; includes acceptance criteria and test plan.
Add instrumentation for queue delay, batch sizes, batch wait time, and per-stage latency; defines metric names and labels for dashboards.
Extend perf-canary to run tiered profiles across key models/GPU SKUs and fail builds on regression thresholds.
Ensure cost-efficient tier interacts correctly with overload protection (load shedding/circuit breakers) and does not increase error rates.
UI/Console engineering task to expose tier dropdown, show computed defaults, and link to docs; includes UX acceptance criteria.
DevEx task to update SDK examples (Python/TS/Go) showing how to choose tiers and override specific batching knobs.
SRE/observability work item for dashboards and alerting per tier; includes rollout monitoring checklist.
Applied ML/evals ticket to gate batching default changes on prompt-set evaluation and define automated rollback signals.
Task to persist tier defaults per model family/variant in the model registry, with versioning and auditability.
Task to ensure Private installer and helm charts handle new tier config; includes migration guide and validation steps.
Release engineering coordination ticket: branch cut, backport policy, CI stability, and release notes checklist for tiered batching.
Follow-up task capturing beta learnings, parameter tuning backlog (by model/GPU), and expansion plan to additional regions.

PR: Implement tier-based scheduler parameter mapping (max_batch, max_queue_delay_ms, prefill/decode weights) behind feature flag.

PR: Fix streaming cadence regression in fast tier by adjusting decode prioritization and adding regression test.
PR: Add config explain endpoint/metadata so Console can display the effective batching defaults and overrides.
PR: Integrate overload protection with cost-efficient tier (backpressure thresholds, load-shed reason codes, dashboards hooks).
PR: Add end-to-end integration tests for tier selection across chat/completions/embeddings routes; includes staging validation steps.
PR: Add perf canary suite jobs that benchmark fast/standard/cost-efficient tiers across top models and fail on p95 regression thresholds.
PR: Add workload corpus runner and reporting template that outputs tier comparison tables ($/token, p95, GPU util).
PR: Store tier defaults per model family (and GPU SKU where needed), with versioning and safe rollout toggles.
PR: Add dashboard JSON definitions for tiered latency/queue delay/batch size views and alerts for canary monitoring.
PR: Customer docs—explain tiers, configuration examples, and trade-offs; includes FAQ and migration guidance.
PR: Update example apps to set batching tier and show how to validate tier behavior via returned headers/metrics.
PR: Python SDK example update—add batching_tier parameter usage and docsstring references; no breaking API changes.
PR: TypeScript SDK examples and config typing updates for batching tier; includes tests for request serialization.
PR: Helm chart values to support tier selection and feature flagging in Private deployments; includes upgrade notes.

PR: Refactor scheduler to make workload signals explicit (prompt length buckets, concurrency) used by tier mapping; includes docs and tests.
PR: Fix memory pressure edge-case in cost-efficient tier (KV cache compaction thresholds) discovered during benchmark runs.
